title: High-Dimensional Minimax Rates for Multimarginal Transport Bounds on Causal Second Moments
banked_reason: The exact all-K minimax and honest-length frontier is not derived: the small-ratio rates, simultaneous all-rematching lower family, and ordered converse remain open, while the sound core proves only the positive-lower-ratio root-N region.
gap_reasons: The proposed exact all-K minimax and honest-length frontier is not derived: this node leaves the small-ratio rate functions, simultaneous all-rematching lower family, and ordered converse open, while the core proves only the positive-lower-ratio root-N region.

Prove a simultaneous-arm indistinguishability lower bound matching the improved upper rate throughout the ratio-to-zero regime, including the exact fixed-K logarithms and an ordered version yielding the matching honest one-sided excess-length converse.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved the sharp residual envelope and optimal-sum-diameter geometry, a dimension-dependent root-N region, honest mean/plugin lower bounds, and a rational certified finite-MOT procedure; the math referee accepted these claims and sources. Attempts via simultaneous-margin finite-support families, two-margin reductions, parity and orthogonal witnesses, and a sharper aggregate dual-process bound did not close the exact small-ratio frontier or its ordered one-sided converse. A future re-raise needs a genuinely new rematching-resistant lower family or shared-geometric upper theorem, not another reframe of the current partial package.
tldr: The lower endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp causal second moment compatible with the \(K\) observed potential-outcome marginals, not a centered-variance endpoint.  On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced arbitrary-margin class, the project proves the sharp residual envelope \(\min\{K,d\}/K^2\), the sharp optimal-sum diameter \(2\sqrt{\min\{K,d\}}\), and a tighter empirical transport upper bound.  These results and an ordered Bernoulli converse give matching root-\(N\) minimax estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length for every fixed \(c_0>0\) along legal arrays with \(K_N\ge c_0N^{q_d}\) eventually, where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\).  The theoretical plug-in lower bound uses an existence-calibrated constant, while the fully specified mean-floor rule depends only on \((\bar X,N,\alpha)\) and requires no transport computation.  Exact rates remain open precisely on the ratio-to-zero subsequences of arrays with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\).  The finite-support lower template is defined but not instantiated: its ordered endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, and strict positive reduced-cost slack against every off-contact rematching column remain certification targets.  A fixed-dimensional rational primal--dual algorithm separately certifies the empirical endpoint.  The STAR audit applies only after the declared known-bound affine scaling, i.i.d. superpopulation assumption, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling; it does not validate the native \(161/37/36\) plug-in calculation.
gap: Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1 gives a high-dimensional empirical bound with term \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\), while Proposition 2 prints a two-margin lower term with \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) and does not establish uniform one-sided coverage or optimal expected excess length. Manole--Niles-Weed leave the same logarithmic all-estimator gap already at two margins. Two-margin entropy transfer and limit theory do not control a growing tuple of jointly conjugate potentials.
fill: The project proves the sharp deterministic residual and support-diameter theorems, uses common-support interpolation to tighten the plug-in rate, settles the large-arm root-\(N\) estimation and one-sided length regimes, and poses the precise coupled-complexity dichotomy whose resolution yields the exact all-\(K\) frontier. Its finite-support handle makes indistinguishability, endpoint separation, and resistance to every rematching column explicit certification targets. The procedure returns a primal--dual numerical bracket, and the STAR audit declares the known bound, affine scaling, superpopulation law, randomization, and balanced subsampling.
